title: A Day That Feels Stuck
description:
For three years, {name} kept to the conventional path.

He divided whatever he earned, sending the portion he could keep into savings and diversified investments. He avoided the big bets. Safe. And slow.

Today {name} saw a post: someone made 100 million won in a single month on crypto. A classmate cleared a year of {name}'s savings in one shot flipping a presale apartment right.

Whenever money came in, {name} divided it in the same order. It was not the wrong road. But some days the numbers on the screen looked like they had stopped moving.

This was the weight of the orthodox path. Boredom. And the doubt — is this really working?

choices.text: Trust the slow road. Slow isn't losing.
choices.result_text: People chasing one big hit also lose it in one. {name} had seen that. Slow isn't losing. Moved the same amount into the same place again.

choices.text: Just once, looked at the risky side
choices.result_text: Just once. Knowing that's exactly how it starts, {name} opened the chart anyway. Heart sped up a little. Better than boredom. That was the scary part.

choices.text: Admitted the weight, and slept early
choices.result_text: Impatience is usually biggest at 3am. {name} turned off the light. Same pace tomorrow. And that's okay — thought it once more before falling asleep.

title: The Chart at 3AM
description:
Three years off the beaten path.

Leverage, day-trading, the seats nobody else takes. The assets swung wildly. Some months doubled. Some months cut in half.

The problem wasn't the money — it was the sleep. Eyes open at 3am. Hand reaches for the phone before the brain does, pulls up the chart. Red and the heart drops; blue and sleep won't come either.

Three years ago this felt like freedom. Now {name} knows — one wrong click can undo everything.

This was the weight of the unorthodox path. Anxiety. And the doubt — is he actually in control of this?

choices.text: This is my way. Stop and you lose.
choices.result_text: Getting this far came from not stopping. {name} chose to believe that. Looked at the chart again. Decided the shaking hands were just the caffeine.

choices.text: Built a safety net. Won't bet it all.
choices.result_text: People who bet everything lose everything. {name} moved a portion somewhere safe. Returns would shrink — but for the first time, slept through the night without waking.

choices.text: Admitted the weight, left the phone in another room
choices.result_text: The chart won't run away. {name} left the phone in the living room and shut the bedroom door. The hand felt empty. Still — fell asleep staring at the ceiling for the first time in a while.

title: A Three-Year Receipt
description:
Out of nowhere, {name} added up the last three years.

Not just the money. The losses had stacked up too, like receipts.

The number of weekend plans turned down. The days a parent's call got cut short. The years a checkup got pushed back. And — the face in the mirror, clearly more worn than three years ago.

Coming this far toward the goal was real. But the road had a price tag, and {name} was only now reading the bill.

choices.text: Knew the cost going in. See it through.
choices.result_text: Nothing's free. {name} knew that starting out. Folded the bill. Stop here and everything paid so far becomes sunk cost.

choices.text: Decided to reclaim one of the things lost
choices.result_text: Can't undo it all, but one was possible. {name} made the call that kept getting pushed back. Or booked the checkup. A small thing. And breathing got a little easier.

choices.text: Stared at the bill a long time. No answer came
choices.result_text: Couldn't tell if it was right or wrong. Only that pretending not to know was no longer an option. That's usually how awareness starts. Uncomfortably.

title: The Bill from Someone You Trusted
description:
By year four, {name} thought he had learned to read people. The man across from him at the pojangmacha was someone he had moved money with more than once, someone whose circumstances he believed he understood.

The man pushed over a thin envelope. The papers asked {name} to cover his share for just one month.

"Just bridge it under your name, hyung."
{name}: "Why does it need my name?"
"Don't you trust me?"

The signature box brought back the blurred name on Father's guarantee PDF. This was no grand fraud and no amount that would ruin him overnight. That made it hurt more. A large betrayal lets you get angry; a hairline crack first makes you doubt your own judgment.

{name} looked from the envelope to the man's face. When a relationship sends a bill, it usually arrives with trust written across the top.

choices.text: Cut them off. A crack never seals back.
choices.result_text: {name} pushed the envelope back and deleted the number. It was not resolve so much as fatigue. Every person he cut off made the world smaller. This time, at least, he had not put his name in someone else's blank.

choices.text: Tried to understand. They must've had reasons.
choices.result_text: He did not sign, but he listened to how the man had reached this point. People rarely set out to become bad. It might have been foolish to keep believing that. Still, understanding someone and guaranteeing them were different acts, and {name} kept that line.

choices.text: Neither hated nor trusted — just kept distance
choices.result_text: He neither cut the man off nor held him close. The envelope went back; the contact stayed. Exactly that much distance. {name} caught himself sorting people by trust rating. He could not tell whether that was adulthood or erosion.

title: The Hand He Did Not Expect
description:
Two days later, Hyunsu's name lit the phone.

"Hyung, have you eaten?"

At the gukbap place in their old goshiwon alley, Hyunsu brought out neither an envelope nor an introduction. When the two stone bowls arrived, he only pushed the kimchi toward {name}.

{name}: "Why call me now?"
Hyunsu: "I can tell from your replies. Your sentences got shorter."
{name}: "You're not here to borrow money, are you?"
Hyunsu: "I called so we wouldn't talk about money. Eat first."

The person he had trusted wanted to borrow his name. The person he had not expected asked for neither name nor reason before offering a hot meal. Help often returned not from the place you had budgeted for it, but from a place you had once held open without noticing.

choices.text: Said thank you properly. With his whole heart.
choices.result_text:
"Thank you, Hyunsu. I mean it."

Hyunsu paused with his spoon raised, then smiled awkwardly. "It's one meal. Eat before it gets cold."

{name} swallowed a spoonful of broth. As the heat moved down his throat, something in his breathing finally loosened.

choices.text: Vowed to repay it. Hates owing.
choices.result_text:
{name} promised he would repay him. Receiving without returning still felt like debt.

Hyunsu shook his head. "Don't pay me back. When you see someone wearing your face someday, buy him dinner."

Perhaps a favor that could not be priced closed its ledger only by moving to someone else.

choices.text: Asked why they were helping
choices.result_text:
"Why are you helping me?"

Hyunsu thought for a long moment. "When I couldn't answer you back then, you didn't rush me. You just stayed."

{name} could not place the exact scene. A silence he had kept without thinking had been a steadying hand for someone. In the fourth year, that hand had come back.

title: That Saying About Money
description:
Even after closing the notebook that held one year of figures, {name} could not sleep. A structure he had not understood a year ago was beginning to show itself across the ledger.

That saying — money attracts money. At first it sounded like a comfort the rich made up. But putting it to work himself, it was real. With 1 million won versus 10 million won, the same rate of return came back at a completely different weight.

And he saw the reverse too. Those with nothing just pay interest until it is over. When the starting lines differ, running at the same speed only widens the gap.

That night, {name} learned that hope and anger could begin with the same number.

description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_reasons_named: In the ledger from that first March, similar amounts belonged to a late finish on one line and the meal that got him through the next day on another. Writing down the reasons had made the structure visible first.
description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_totals_only: That first March, he had reconciled the total and stopped there. The figures were exact; only a full year of entries revealed why equal amounts could carry different weight.

choices.text: Understand the system and ride it
choices.result_text: Cursing an unfair world and understanding the system to use it are two different things. {name} chose the latter. Anger he'd keep only as fuel.

choices.text: Ride it, but never forget the starting lines differed
choices.result_text: If he ever climbed up, he didn't want to become someone who forgot the days of just paying interest at the bottom. {name} wrote the vow down somewhere. Because forgetting was a sure thing.

choices.text: Honestly, the anger was bigger
choices.result_text: Why does one person start with 10 million won and another with 1 million won? {name} knew there was no answer and still held the question a long while. Anger was energy too.

title: Doors Are Opened by People
description:
Nine at night. Only folding chairs remained in the common meeting room after a free public briefing. No one had invited {name} personally. Near the exit, strangers checked the schedule and exchanged contact details while the organizer gathered a few blank visitor cards.

{name} held only the public schedule and one card with no name on it. Opportunity clearly moved through people, but no one he met tonight could yet be called an opportunity.

The elevator was about to close. The organizer had shouldered their bag, and the ride home was enough time to finish the file he had postponed. {name} had one move left to make.

choices.text: Tell the three people by the elevator his name first
choices.result_text: {name} held the closing door and introduced himself and his work. Two people shared their contact details; another named the next public session. The earlier train left without him, and the file in his bag remained unfinished.

choices.text: Ask the organizer for the admission rules and costs first
choices.result_text: The organizer wrote down which meetings were public, which were paid, and who chose the attendees. The elevator closed during the explanation. No contacts were gained, but the conditions for entering were now on paper.

choices.text: Return the visitor card and go prepare alone
choices.result_text: {name} returned the blank card and headed for the station. No new contact entered his phone. On the train, however, he finished the last page of the postponed file. Whether tonight's seat would open again remained unknown.

title: The Source of the First Repayment
description:
At 11:21 p.m., {name} opened the repayment screen for one amount carried over from last month. The original amount, the first installment due tonight, and the balance that would remain occupied separate lines. One fee, however, was labeled only ‘processing.’

Sending the agreed amount before midnight would keep the first deadline. Asking again could reveal who received which money, but the transfer window might close while he waited. Sending only principal would leave a reason on record, along with an unpaid mark.

The cursor waited in the transfer memo. The word repayment could not close both the source of the amount and the responsibility still left behind.

choices.text: Have them read out principal, fees, and balance before sending the agreed first amount
choices.result_text:
{name} called the listed contact and asked for all three lines to be read aloud. After confirming who received the processing fee and what balance would remain, he transferred only the agreed first installment.

The completion time was four minutes after midnight. The call record and transfer receipt stayed together, but the first installment now carried a late mark. The first deadline passed while he secured the source of the explanation.

choices.text: Keep the deadline first and name the source and installment in the transfer memo
choices.result_text:
{name} sent the displayed first installment and wrote the original transaction and ‘installment one’ in the memo. The completion mark appeared before midnight.

He still did not know who received the processing fee. He attached the receipt to last month's ledger without erasing the line whose explanation remained blank.

choices.text: Send principal without the processing fee and leave a written objection
choices.result_text:
{name} transferred the agreed principal portion and wrote, ‘I will review the processing fee when I receive its basis.’ A principal receipt appeared, but the account status stayed ‘partially unpaid.’

The other side left only a read mark. {name} recorded the reduced balance and the unresolved fee in the same ledger box.

title: The Small Print on the Limit Sheet
description:
At 4:40 p.m., the printer at the bank desk pushed out a preliminary limit estimate. The number at the top was larger than {name} had expected. Below it, smaller lines listed rate changes, income verification, and reasons for rejection.

The banker highlighted the preliminary maximum. “This estimates what may be approved. It is neither what you can carry nor an official limit.” The monthly payment looked manageable against current income. The box for one month of reduced income was still blank.

Twelve minutes remained. {name} could use them for a risk worksheet, lower his own ceiling and receive an official sheet, or take an official sheet at the preliminary maximum.

choices.text: Add rejection conditions and the payment after an income drop
choices.result_text:
The banker printed a separate risk worksheet with three lines: job loss, reduced income, and a higher rate. The payment beneath the preliminary maximum changed three times.

{name} circled the amount in the worst month. The appointment ended before an official limit sheet could be issued. He left without the large number, but the first point of failure now existed on paper.

choices.text: Recalculate using only what his own current income can repay
choices.result_text:
{name} asked the banker to recalculate from his currently verified income and the amount he could still repay after one reduced-income month. The new limit fell sharply below the first number.

The banker placed both sheets side by side. {name} dated the smaller one. The amount he could be responsible for became clearer than the amount he could obtain.

choices.text: Take the official maximum-limit sheet but do not apply today
choices.result_text:
{name} had an official limit sheet issued at the preliminary maximum and signed only the explanation acknowledgment. He left the application blank. The banker highlighted the sheet's validity date once more.

He left with a document he could use immediately, but without the risk worksheet. No money had entered the account. Only the deadline for deciding again was clear.

title: Across from the Introducer
description:
At 5:03 p.m., {name}, Sangchul, and an introducer he had never met sat across from one another in Sangchul's office. The page on the table printed only the projected return in bold. The boxes for the source of the money and the recipient of the introduction fee were empty.

Sangchul pushed over a cup of cold instant coffee. “If you write every name first, the good seats are already gone. You enter by judging the person.” The introducer pinned down the corner of the sheet but did not offer a name.

Fifteen minutes remained before the next appointment. Asking about the source, forcing the costs onto paper, or stopping at the blank terms would each leave a different loss.

choices.text: Make both men write their names and identify who supplies the money
choices.result_text:
{name} pointed to the two blank boxes. The introducer produced a card; Sangchul wrote only the funding company's name. The pen stopped when {name} asked for the individual behind it.

The next appointment time passed. The answer was incomplete, but the paper and card now showed exactly who had refused to write a name.

choices.text: Have them itemize the introduction fee and every later charge
choices.result_text:
The introducer first called it ‘customary.’ When {name} pushed over a blank page, the man separated an opening fee, materials, and a success charge. Sangchul stirred the cold coffee.

By the time three cost lines and their billing dates existed, the time to leave for the next address had passed. The cost sheet remained, but the individual funder's name was still blank, and that day's next door had closed.

choices.text: Say there will be no next meeting without written terms
choices.result_text:
{name} left the sheet unfolded at the center of the table. “I won't go to the next address while those boxes are blank.”

The introducer stood first. Sangchul did not stop him. No next address arrived from this meeting. What remained on {name}'s phone was a photograph of the blank boxes and the time the man left.

title: The Name Behind the Card
description:
A temporary site office occupied the second floor of a shopping block marked for demolition. Redevelopment plans covered the walls; zone passes and hard hats lay across folding tables. Before the attendees, Sangchul rested a hand lightly on {name}'s shoulder.

"I brought this man."

The introducer column already read ‘Lim Sangchul’ beside {name}'s name. Nothing stated what the visit would demand later or whether the next seat carried a charge. The site coordinator said the elevator would leave soon with a small group for one zone. Sangchul fanned three passes in one hand.

"Questions come after you get inside."

{name} had to decide whether to demand terms first, narrow the visit, or stop at an unwritten condition.

choices.text: Ask about the introducer and costs in front of everyone
choices.result_text: {name} pointed to the attendance sheet and asked them to write down who introduced whom and which later costs could arise. While the coordinator added two lines, the elevator left. The terms remained on paper; the first site walk did not.

choices.text: Accept one person's pass for one zone only
choices.result_text: {name} chose one coordinator and one zone to inspect. Sangchul collected the other two passes. The broad introduction disappeared, but who he was meeting and where they were going stayed clear to the end.

choices.text: Return the pass unless the terms are written down
choices.result_text:
When Sangchul did not answer, {name} placed the pass back on the table and asked for ‘entry declined because terms were not disclosed’ to be written beside his name. The coordinator added the reason to the visit record and let him photograph that line.

The safety briefing began and the group moved through the inner door. {name} lost the site walk, but kept one record showing that he had not entered under unexplained terms.

title: Under Her Name
description:
At the entrance to a private Gangnam housing briefing, the clerk checked the list twice and could not find {name}. Jiyeon showed the invitation on her phone, and the clerk took out one wristband.

"We can register him as one guest accompanying Han Jiyeon."

The desk screen displayed ‘Han Jiyeon — one guest’ first. Jiyeon did not sign for him. She pushed the pen toward {name}.

"I opened this door, Minjun. You decide what you say inside. Just don't pretend my name was never used to bring you here."

Eight minutes remained before the first session. {name} could reintroduce himself under his own name, ask what Jiyeon's family would expect to hear, or leave the wristband and keep only the conversation between them.

choices.text: Erase the guest label and explain his own name and work
choices.result_text: Before accepting the wristband, {name} asked the clerk to remove the guest label. The first entry line began moving while he explained his name and work from the beginning. The clerk issued a separate waiting number. He missed the first session, but the next-session list carried his own name. Jiyeon waited beside the empty desk without rushing him.

choices.text: Ask what Jiyeon's family would expect before going in
choices.result_text: Jiyeon darkened her screen. "Father doesn't know yet. When he does, he'll ask why you came here, Minjun." They did not rehearse an answer. The first session passed while the wristband stayed on the counter.

choices.text: Decline the wristband and talk with Jiyeon outside
choices.result_text: {name} returned the guest wristband and moved to a bench beyond the lobby. He missed the presentation. When he asked why she had used her name, Jiyeon answered, "I hated rooms filled only with Father's choices. If you came in, at least one person there would be someone I chose."

title: At the Casino Door
description:
At the Jeongseon casino entrance, the shuttle attendant opened the reservation list. Beside {name}'s name was ‘Lim Sangchul's party,’ but Sangchul had gone in ahead and did not answer his phone. The attendant handed over a temporary pass and pointed to a table number inside.

"Your group has already exchanged its cash. They're starting soon."

Beyond the glass, people addressed one another by industry and title. Entering without asking who shared the table could settle the relationship before the money moved. Across the lobby stood the cashier and the lockers. The last shuttle to Seoul would leave in thirty minutes. {name} could not keep the pass, all the cash he brought, and the ride home at once.

choices.text: Ask for the names and relationships at the table before entering
choices.result_text: The attendant reopened the list and identified three people and each connection to Sangchul. During the explanation, one reserved seat went to another guest. {name} remained outside with the pass, while every bill he brought stayed untouched.

choices.text: Keep only the cash he can afford to lose and lock away the rest
choices.result_text: {name} took out only the amount set in advance and locked the wallet and remaining cash away. On the exchange receipt, he wrote the number at which he would stop. The door opened, but the locker key kept its weight in his pocket.

choices.text: Return the pass and take the last shuttle to Seoul
choices.result_text: {name} gave the pass back and crossed to the bus bay. He sent Sangchul one line: "I'm not going in tonight." The cash stayed folded. When the bus door closed, the casino lights began to recede.

title: A Time Already Past
description:
At 11:43 p.m., one calendar alert had faded gray. It held the address and visit time for the one place {name} could actually have reached today. No arrival record carried his name.

The person who sent the address had left one short message: ‘Today's session has ended.’ Beneath it sat the end time and confirmation number for the paid shift {name} had kept instead. One side of the screen held an address he had not reached; the other held work he had actually finished on the same date.

Choosing no door had still spent the day. Now he had to decide how to record the missed promise: apologize directly, keep the address and time as an open record, or keep only the completed shift and close the contact route too.

choices.text: Contact one person and apologize for not going today
choices.result_text: {name} named that place and time and apologized without an excuse. The only reply was, "Today's session has ended." No new date followed. At least one ignored conversation moved from the bottom of the screen to the top.

choices.text: Record the missed address, time, and ‘did not arrive’
choices.result_text: {name} wrote ‘did not arrive’ beside that address and time. A blank that was neither profit nor expense became a record for the first time. No message went out, and the completed-shift confirmation remained on its separate line.

choices.text: Keep only the completed shift and close the missed address and contact thread in the archive
choices.result_text:
{name} attached only the paid-shift confirmation to the ledger. He moved the gray address notice and its conversation into an archive labeled ‘Closed Doors’ and removed them from the first screen.

What he had missed on the day he protected his income survived only in the archive title. This month's record kept neither an address to revisit nor an open thread in which to apologize.

title: The Introduction's Second Bill
description:
At 11:36 p.m., the itemized bill for last month's redevelopment visit filled the payment screen. The travel charge, materials, the one zone {name} had actually entered, and the coordinator's name all matched. The last line, ‘network management,’ named neither the work nor its recipient.

Paying in full before midnight would avoid an overdue mark. Calling the coordinator could verify some items, but the deadline might pass while he waited. Removing the unexplained line would cost less and leave an objection on record, along with an open balance.

{name} matched the pass number to the invoice and pressed the transfer amount again. One door had returned as three separate charges.

choices.text: Have the coordinator read each item and pay only the verified charges
choices.result_text:
{name} called the site coordinator and matched the dates for travel and materials one by one. Midnight passed during the explanation of the management fee, but he transferred the two verified amounts.

The bill remained ‘partially paid.’ Beside the call record, two explained lines and one line without a basis stayed visibly separate.

choices.text: Pay in full before the deadline and preserve the original invoice
choices.result_text:
{name} paid all three items and stored the completion screen beside the original invoice. It was eleven minutes before midnight.

No overdue mark appeared. The meaning of ‘network management’ remained blank, however. The payment closed; the question moved behind the receipt.

choices.text: Remove the unexplained fee and send the rest with a written objection
choices.result_text:
{name} paid only travel and materials and wrote, ‘Please identify the service and recipient for the management fee.’ The coordinator read it without replying.

Only the verified amount left the account. One unpaid line remained on the invoice, and {name} captured it together with the written objection.

title: Before the Person Who Waited
description:
At 9:18 p.m. in the express-bus terminal, the coordinator from last month's site sat across from {name}. Their review appointment had begun thirty-eight minutes earlier; the coffee in the paper cup had gone cold. The coordinator opened no new materials.

“If you couldn't make the agreed time, did you at least know whose name held the seat?”

On {name}'s phone, Sangchul's address, the time he had read it, and the record of the other work he had actually finished remained separate. Showing everything would explain the delay and hand over another person's name. Naming only his own choice would preserve responsibility and conceal part of the cause. Apologizing without asking for another date would return the power to reopen the relationship to the person who had waited.

choices.text: Show Sangchul's address and the actual times, then explain from the beginning
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the phone on the table and showed Sangchul's address, the time he had seen it, and the order in which the delay happened. The coordinator paused at Sangchul's name.

“Now I know why. I'll decide whether to contact you for another review.” No new date was set. The explanation and the time spent waiting remained beside the cold coffee.

choices.text: Leave out other names and say only what he chose first
choices.result_text:
{name} did not open anyone else's message. “I finished something else first, and I also failed to warn you in time.”

The coordinator asked for no further reason and wrote ‘thirty-eight minutes late’ on the appointment sheet. One name stayed private; an empty part of the explanation stayed too. No new date was offered.

choices.text: Apologize without asking for another date
choices.result_text:
{name} named the late time and the waiting he had caused, then apologized without an excuse. “Whether we meet again should be your decision.”

The coordinator threw away the paper cup and stood. No answer and no new appointment remained. On the terminal bench, only {name} and the original meeting time were left.

title: How Far to Erase the Next Seat
description:
At 8:50 p.m., Sangchul sent the address and seat number for the next private dinner. Beneath ‘the same people as last time,’ the reply deadline sat ten minutes away. {name}'s calendar already held one more repeating invitation at the same hour.

Canceling only tonight would leave the channel open. Asking to be removed from the invitation list could also cut off the next proposal. Refusing every seat until written terms arrived would close the door and leave a reason on record.

No typing indicator appeared in Sangchul's chat. After ‘I can't come,’ {name} had to decide in his own words how much else to close.

choices.text: Cancel only this seat and say he will review future proposals separately
choices.result_text:
{name} named the date and seat number and declined only this invitation. Sangchul replied, “Understood. We'll look at the next one separately.”

A strike appeared through tonight's address. The conversation and the route for another proposal remained open; only one seat had closed.

choices.text: Ask for his name to be removed from the repeating invitation list
choices.result_text:
{name} asked to be removed not only from tonight's seat but from the list that kept bringing the same group together. Sangchul read it at once and did not answer for a long time.

After the deadline, four words arrived: “I'll do that, then.” The address disappeared, and no next date stayed pinned above the conversation.

choices.text: Refuse every seat until the terms arrive in writing
choices.result_text:
{name} asked for the introducer, fees, and attendance terms in writing and said he would not attend tonight or any later seat before receiving them.

Sangchul replied, “You've grown fond of paper.” The address vanished from the calendar, but no document arrived. The reason for canceling and an empty attachment box remained on the same screen.

title: Three Places, One Weekend
description:
Saturday, four in the afternoon. {name} had arrived for his plans with Daeun and Sangchul's contract review. Daeun set down two canned coffees from the convenience store where they first met. Sangchul wrote one hour on the meeting sheet, then opened the source terms beside the financing-gap table.

"Didn't expect you to read the terms too, Daeun."

She folded one cardigan cuff. "I came to be beside Minjun. That doesn't mean he gave me the questions."

A voice message from Father arrived: ‘Hospital's done. If you're busy, forget it.’ The unselected weekend promise already carried a time that had passed.

Sangchul laid his watch beside the papers. "The review has started. Decide what gets exposed first." Daeun left the dent in her can. The terms, the gap, and Father's name reflected in the glass tabletop.

choices.text: Give Daeun the right to choose the risk clauses
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the highlighter before Daeun. "Choose the first three lines we read."

She marked early recovery, joint liability, and an unexplained fee. Sangchul began the first line, then turned his watch facedown. "Hand over the questions too, and we won't finish the figures today."

They got three meanings and lost twenty-one minutes of negotiation. Only Daeun's yellow lines remained on the terms.

choices.text: Expose the financing gap before anything else
choices.result_text:
{name} turned the gap table around before the terms. He pointed to what his money could not cover and the amount needed by next month.

Daeun read it twice and took her hand off the can. "So this was the part you didn't want me to see, not the clauses." Sangchul leaned back without a word.

The review continued, but a private fact about their means now lay before Sangchul too. One corner of the table darkened in cold coffee.

choices.text: Acknowledge the missed promise to Father before both of them
choices.result_text:
{name} did not play the message. He turned its timestamp toward them. "I didn't choose the hospital promise today, and I missed it. I won't rename that as being busy."

Sangchul put his watch back on. "Family business doesn't need to enter the minutes." Daeun answered softly, "Minjun chose to enter it."

The review clock kept running. One private line {name} had hidden occupied the first blank in the minutes.

title: The Right to Correct
description:
Saturday, four in the afternoon. {name} entered Sangchul's review room at the time promised to Jiyeon. She removed her watch and set it on the table, then compared the company name on the source terms with the issuer on the gap table.

Sangchul stirred instant coffee. "I don't need the details between you two. Let's stay with the numbers."

"The names attached to numbers are facts too, sir." Without smiling, Jiyeon tapped one incorrect title. "Separate sales language from contract language."

A missed notice from Father's finished appointment remained on {name}'s phone. The lost hour, the review clock, and his plans with Jiyeon occupied one frame. Sangchul started the timer. Jiyeon kept the papers open and asked which fact they would expose together first.

choices.text: Give Jiyeon the first question
choices.result_text:
{name} moved his notes aside. "Choose the first question, Jiyeon."

She asked when liability ended, not how profits began. Sangchul redirected twice; she repeated the same question with only the date changed. The third answer finally produced one termination condition.

They had an answer and sixteen minutes left. Jiyeon capped her pen. "The questions didn't consume the time. Avoiding them twice did."

choices.text: Put the gap and his own funds before Jiyeon
choices.result_text:
{name} turned the gap table toward Jiyeon without covering his own-funds column. Sangchul began, "You two can look at that privately—" but Jiyeon left it in place.

"Don't speak as if my money fills this." She wrote one question mark beside the gap.

{name} could no longer hide his means from Sangchul. All three gazes stopped on the same empty column.

choices.text: Stop where fact and sales language split
choices.result_text:
{name} covered the phrase ‘safely secured.’ "We don't read past this line until it has a source."

Sangchul pointed to the timer. "Then this is where today's review time ends." Jiyeon closed the document and wrote down the closing time in her own notebook.

Nothing was approved and the remaining negotiation window was gone. Jiyeon's exact timestamp remained on the folded terms.

title: A Witness Through the Speaker
description:
{name} sat alone with the deal lead. The family appointment was now a gray calendar square; there had never been a romance appointment. He had arrived on time for the selected investment review. The lead set a document bag on the empty chair and opened the terms.

Hyunsu's voice message waited on the phone. Asked to check only the dates and labels in the material, Hyunsu had separated what he could see from what he did not know. The lead lowered a paper cup at the sight of the play button.

"Bring a friend in and your weakness comes with him. You know that, right?"

Hyunsu's name sat above 1:12. Playing everything would expose {name}'s circumstances; quoting facts alone could hide who checked them. One notice from the missed family promise waited silently below.

choices.text: Play Hyunsu's whole message, including the weakness
choices.result_text:
{name} switched on the speaker. After the dates, Hyunsu also said why {name} seemed pressed to accept the terms. The deal lead began taking notes from that hesitation before the factual difference.

The discrepancy was clear when the message ended, and so was {name}'s pressure. The lead moved the paper cup onto the empty chair.

choices.text: Read only the dates and labels Hyunsu verified
choices.result_text:
{name} did not play the audio. He read the two labels and dates Hyunsu had checked. "I won't name the person today. This is the limit of the verification."

The deal lead asked for the source three times, stopping the reading each time. Hyunsu's name stayed private; the verification carried only half its weight. The unplayed waveform remained on-screen.

choices.text: Name Hyunsu and state the exact limit of his check
choices.result_text:
{name} showed the message header instead of pressing play. "Hyunsu Kim checked only the dates and labels. I did not ask for judgment or investment."

The deal lead wrote Hyunsu into the meeting notes. {name} immediately added the limit, but a third party's name had already entered the record. The audio stayed unheard; only the exposure cost remained in ink.

title: Daeun at Two A.M.
description:
At two in the morning, {name} opened the door fully after the third ring. Daeun stepped one foot across the threshold, still holding a convenience-store bag. She took in the sweat-soaked shirt, the overturned cup, and the shaking hand without touching him.

"Minjun, don't call what I'm seeing fine."

When {name} braced against the wall, Daeun's hand rose and stopped in the air. "Can I hold your arm? Or should I stay here?"

The laptop showed the timestamp when the symptoms began beside an unopened help screen. Daeun did not power it off or contact anyone for him. She opened a water bottle and left it by the threshold. The corridor light went dark and bright through the open door. He could no longer hide the shaking; he could still decide how much care to place in her hands.

choices.text: Give Daeun permission to hold his arm
choices.result_text:
"Below the elbow. Don't pull me up at once."

Daeun touched only the place {name} named. The warmth through his shirt made the shaking more visible. She asked slowly, as if counting, "How many minutes has the dizziness lasted?"

He lost the dignity of standing alone. Daeun did not move an inch beyond the permission he gave.

choices.text: Show only the timestamp and screen, refusing touch
choices.result_text:
{name} turned the laptop toward her. "My hands started shaking at 1:42. You can see the screen, but please don't touch me."

Daeun lowered her hand and read only the work log and the title of the unopened help page. "All right. Then I won't accept the word fine from you right now either."

He surrendered the private timestamp and kept the boundary of touch. Daeun placed both hands beside the opened bottle.

choices.text: Ask Daeun directly to remain at the threshold
choices.result_text:
"Don't come farther in. Stay there while I settle my breathing. If I need more, I'll ask first."

Daeun sat on the threshold with the bag on her knees. She made no call and pressed no clock on him. {name} leaned against the wall and counted his breaths from one.

The request for help carried into the hall. The open door and one step of distance remained between them.

title: Half a Second at the Threshold
description:
At two in the morning, Jiyeon checked the entryway clock before greeting {name}. Her coat was fastened as neatly as ever, and her phone already held the time she arrived. "Minjun, answer briefly from here. When did this start?"

{name}'s hand slipped from the door handle. Jiyeon stepped forward by reflex and stopped exactly. Half a second to reach out, half a second to draw back.

"I should ask before I touch you." Her voice stayed level, though the last syllable split slightly.

An unbroken cup and spilled water lay on the floor; the screen held the onset time. Jiyeon contacted no one and stood just inside the open door. A person who wanted to put everything in order and one who wanted nothing seen now shared the same threshold.

choices.text: State the onset time and allow Jiyeon to hold his wrist
choices.result_text:
{name} gave the exact time and held out his wrist. "You may. I still decide what happens next."

Jiyeon used two fingers and watched the second hand. She asked nothing else while counting, then recorded only the time.

The body's measure passed to her; the decision did not. One stroke beneath her neat writing trembled.

choices.text: Show the screen and ask her not to touch him
choices.result_text:
{name} turned over the work log and symptom timestamp. "You can see this much. Please don't touch me."

Jiyeon nodded and stepped back. "Understood. I'll separate what I know from what I'm guessing too."

His work hours and shaking were exposed; no touch occurred. Jiyeon's hand clenched only inside her coat pocket.

choices.text: Ask her to stay without deciding for him
choices.result_text:
"Don't call or organize anything for me. Stay here until I can speak."

Jiyeon closed her notes and sat on the entryway floor. "All right. But the time you spend not speaking is still something I witnessed."

The controlling hand rested empty on her knee. {name} had asked for help, and only the arrival time remained in their silence.

title: Hyung, Leave the Door Open
description:
At two in the morning, Hyunsu reached the open door and caught his breath against the corridor rail. He held convenience-store water and a charging cable. "Hyung, can I come in? I can stay here too."

{name} moved only his lips. His fingertips shook; a tight line ran from his left temple into his neck. Hyunsu did not cover it with a joke as he once might have in the goshiwon. He looked at the clock and overturned cup, took out his phone, then set it down without waking the screen.

"Tell me when it started and where it feels wrong. I won't say I handled it for you."

The door was already open. Hyunsu waited one step outside for what {name} would hand over: the boundary between leaning on a friend and the shame of explaining his own body.

choices.text: Give the exact onset time and location of the pain
choices.result_text:
{name} checked the clock and stated the time and location in separate sentences. Hyunsu copied them into his phone without adding a guess.

"I wrote exactly what you said, hyung. Nothing else."

The coordinates of the body passed into a friend's hand while the lock screen stayed private. No blank remained between Hyunsu's two lines.

choices.text: Hand Hyunsu the unlocked phone
choices.result_text:
{name} unlocked the phone and held it out on the call screen. "Only what we need. Don't open the other chats."

Hyunsu took it in both hands and lowered the brightness. "Understood. I won't go farther than you said."

The means of contact and a door into private life passed together. Hyunsu's thumb stopped at the edge without pressing a name.

choices.text: Leave the door open and ask him to watch from one step away
choices.result_text:
"Don't come in. Watch from there until I can move."

Hyunsu stepped back toward the rail and put down the water. "Call and I'll come right in. If you don't, I'll stay here."

{name} kept the distance but could no longer say he was alone. Whenever the corridor sensor went dark, Hyunsu moved one foot to bring the light back.

title: A Future at the Same Table
description:
{name} and Daeun arrived together at the restaurant Father chose. Three bowls of soup waited, but no one lifted a spoon. Father's factory-hardened fingers rolled the handle slowly.

"Daeun, will you keep living in Seoul to fit Minjun's plan?"

Daeun set down her glass. "That makes me sound attached to his plan, Father."

When {name} tried to step in, she raised a palm. "Minjun, let me answer."

Father looked into his soup. "At a hospital door and at the door to his own body, he tries to decide alone. I fear he'll do it even with someone beside him."

Daeun folded one cardigan cuff, remembering the door opened before dawn. "I fear the conclusion coming first too. But don't decide my answer for me."

Both looked at {name}. The steam above the soup was almost gone.

choices.text: Ask Father to say what frightens him first
choices.result_text:
{name} turned toward Father instead of answering. "Don't tell us how I should live yet. Tell me what you're afraid of."

Father put down the spoon. "I'm afraid you'll believe money means you no longer owe people an explanation."

Daeun did not interrupt. Father's pride lowered, and fear rather than advice entered the space between the bowls.

choices.text: Acknowledge the hospital-door choice without making it noble
choices.result_text:
{name} read what he had done at that door exactly as it remained in the record. Whether it was a visit, a delay, or avoidance, he did not rename it as being for Father.

Father asked, "And you're telling me now?" Daeun watched {name}. "At least this time you said it before both of us."

The shame remained and the fact did not hide. Ceiling light lay white on the cooling soup.

choices.text: Ask Daeun's boundary before Father's expectations
choices.result_text:
{name} asked Daeun, "Which questions do you want to answer here? I won't decide first."

She turned the glass once. "My work and family plans. I won't answer whether we combine money or where we live today." Father's mouth tightened.

{name} repeated the boundary aloud. Father's expectations were cut short; Daeun's place setting remained.

title: Three People's Right to Correct
description:
{name} and Jiyeon reached the restaurant Father had chosen three minutes early. She hung her coat and aligned the three water glasses. Father closed the menu. "If you're staying in Seoul, are you two planning to live together?"

Jiyeon did not smile. "We have not decided that I will stay or promised one home. We came to say which costs we will not hide, Father."

Father's brow rose. "Those are very tidy words. People don't live by a table."

"That is why facts and expectations need separate columns." Jiyeon wrote ‘hospital, Seoul, relationship’ on a napkin. No one had said what happened at the hospital door, and no future had been agreed. The three had reached the same table without deciding who could correct the questions.

choices.text: Give Jiyeon the right to correct dates and facts
choices.result_text:
{name} told Father, "If I say it wrong, let Jiyeon correct me immediately."

Beside cohabitation, moving, and shared money, Jiyeon drew blanks where no agreement existed. Father stopped twice and began his sentence again.

The table slowed. {name} lost the room to polish the story. More blanks than answers remained on the napkin.

choices.text: Expose family cost and romance cost in the same terms
choices.result_text:
{name} named the time withheld from Father and the time postponed with Jiyeon without placing them on different scales. "Both are costs I made. I won't use one to excuse the other."

Father set down his chopsticks. "You put family and romance on one line?" Jiyeon did not erase the sentence.

The family hierarchy shook, and {name} lost the dignity of avoiding comparison. Both water glasses trembled at once.

choices.text: Set Jiyeon's consent boundary before Father's future questions
choices.result_text:
{name} asked Jiyeon first, "How far may we answer tonight?"

"Current costs and the hospital door. Not marriage, a home, or a name." Father swallowed the question he had prepared.

{name} drew a line beneath the three words. Father's curiosity remained; Jiyeon's scope was confirmed in public. One pair of chopsticks stayed wrapped.

title: Soup Set for Two
description:
Saturday evening, {name} arrived alone at a restaurant promised to an actual family member. Two bowls of soup and two sets of dishes waited; no coat hung on the empty chair. He had not selected the action of bringing a partner. That proved neither that there was no relationship nor that anyone had refused.

The relative filled the glasses. "You came alone. Am I not hearing about the person beside you in Seoul today?"

{name} turned his phone facedown. The round-trip time and fare were visible; no other commitment's completion or loss could be known here.

"I want to know why you came alone, not why somebody isn't here." Steam from the two bowls met in the center. {name} had to own only the choice to come alone, without making another person's absence an excuse.

choices.text: Say coming without a partner was his own choice
choices.result_text:
"I chose to come alone today. I won't say the other person refused."

The relative lowered the glass. "Then those aren't words you agreed on together either." {name} said no.

He owned the absence without gaining a right to explain the relationship. No name was attached to the empty chair.

choices.text: Answer only the hospital-door fact and refuse relationship questions
choices.result_text:
{name} described what he had done at the hospital door only to the recorded limit. When the relative asked again about the person beside him, he shook his head. "I won't discuss them while they're absent."

The relative said, "Not even with me?" but stopped. One factual line opened and the relationship door stayed shut. Oil slowly set on the soup.

choices.text: Show the Saturday time and fare spent on this table
choices.result_text:
{name} read the departure time and round-trip fare from the receipt. "This is the time and money I cleared for today. I won't invent another job I lost."

The relative listened longer to the last sentence than the amount. "Then eat before you go."

Time and money were verified; exaggerating another sacrifice was closed off. The receipt lay unfolded between the bowls.

title: The Table Never Set
description:
Saturday night, two finished times remained gray in {name}'s calendar. He had selected neither facing family nor bringing a partner to the table. No restaurant soup, opposite chair, or attendee's expression therefore existed.

His phone held an unfinished line to family—‘I won't make it today’—and the passed time that a companion's place would have required him to explain. The record did not name the partner or include what they exchanged that day.

{name} opened the monthly ledger at his empty desk. Neither commitment had a completion mark. An excuse might reach one relative while leaving the other absence untouched. Sending nothing would avoid inventing a person and make the silence part of his record. The monitor clock kept adding minutes beyond both promises.

choices.text: Send family one line of absence without an excuse
choices.result_text:
{name} deleted every reason and sent only: ‘I did not come to today's appointment. I'm sorry I did not say so earlier.’

He did not check for a read mark or reply. One line reached family; no person was attached to the other expiration. The sent time appeared beneath the gray appointment.

choices.text: Record only the times when both places passed
choices.result_text:
{name} entered the family appointment and the companion-action deadline separately. He wrote no imagined sentence about who might have been there. The unsent family draft remained on his phone.

No explanation reached anyone; only the dates became exact. The same word, ‘incomplete,’ ended both lines. The pen marks were heavy without a name.

choices.text: Send no draft and confirm both expirations as they are
choices.result_text:
{name} deleted the message and copied both expiration times into the ledger. He added neither ‘busy’ nor ‘next time.’

No reaction was created and no late apology opened. When the phone went dark, only two gray squares remained in the room.

title: The Blank for a Name
description:
Sangchul placed the review terms beneath the financing gap they had already measured. The proposed co-obligor box was blank; the next page showed the lower ceiling available under {name}'s name alone. Daeun pulled both pages toward her.

"Daeun's name preserves the scale. We aren't asking for it today, only whether you will keep reviewing."

She moved between early recovery and joint liability. "Show me where I can refuse and the full range I would carry. Don't tell me it is unlikely."

{name} had disclosed the terms and could ask only for willingness to continue. No signature, consent, or filing had occurred. Sangchul pushed away his cold coffee. Daeun left the pen untouched and asked who would choose the questions and which number would be exposed first.

choices.text: Give Daeun the right to mark the refusal clauses
choices.result_text:
{name} put the highlighter before Daeun. "Choose the clauses where review must stop."

She marked changes to guarantee scope, early recovery, and added costs. Sangchul began explaining the first; his prepared return table slid aside.

{name} lost control of the order and Daeun drew her own line. No name or signature appeared in the yellow marks.

choices.text: Make Sangchul read the joint-liability language verbatim
choices.result_text:
{name} covered the summary and asked Sangchul to read the liability paragraph from the start. He included ‘maximum’ and ‘exceptions.’

Daeun asked, "Why was this one sentence when you explained it?" Sangchul did not answer at once.

They heard the scope, and the couple's private finances opened in the same room. Only the terms remained spread beside the cold coffee.

choices.text: Reveal his lower solo ceiling and ask only whether to keep reviewing
choices.result_text:
{name} read aloud the ceiling possible under his name alone. "This number is mine. Today I am asking only whether you want to keep reading these terms."

Daeun studied the smaller figure without folding a corner. "I'll make a question list. Any answer comes after that."

The reduced scale lay exposed and only the review window remained. The box stayed blank.

title: A Deadline Before the Name
description:
Sangchul placed the financing-gap table and joint-liability review copy before Jiyeon. The lower ceiling under {name}'s name alone had already been measured. Jiyeon checked page numbers and issue times without touching the blank name box.

"We need no signature today, only whether to continue reviewing," {name} said.

Sangchul smiled. "There isn't time to read every condition before an answer. Let's take the important ones."

Jiyeon centered the copy. "Who decides importance? The person borrowing a name and the person lending one won't rank it the same way." Her honorifics stayed precise; the pen cap closed sharply.

There was no signature, consent, or filing. What remained was the question order, {name}'s actual ceiling, and the right not to answer today.

choices.text: Give Jiyeon the first question and the right to correct
choices.result_text:
{name} turned his list facedown. "Choose the first question and correct anything wrong."

Jiyeon asked when joint liability began. Each time Sangchul said ‘roughly,’ she pointed back to the date in the terms.

Half the review time disappeared and control passed to Jiyeon. Three dates, not a name, occupied the blank.

choices.text: Expose his solo ceiling and financing gap first
choices.result_text:
{name} put the lower ceiling and remaining gap on one screen. "I won't ask you to continue while hiding this difference."

Jiyeon read it. "Then call my name a separate risk, not the solution." Sangchul's smile vanished.

The weakness opened before both of them and one sales phrase was crossed out. The gap remained.

choices.text: Refuse an answer today and set only a copy-and-question deadline
choices.result_text:
{name} gave Jiyeon the review copy and asked only when questions would arrive. She wrote seven tomorrow evening. "I'll send questions then. I am not answering whether I continue."

Sangchul warned that today's window would shrink. {name} did not press her. Current negotiation time was lost; only the copy and deadline entered Jiyeon's bag.

title: The Co-Obligor Box Left Blank
description:
Before the deal lead, {name} finished measuring the ceiling and gap under his name alone. The co-obligor box remained blank, and no other person's name entered the room today. The document could not say whether that came from consent not chosen or from having no relationship whose name could be borrowed.

The lead pushed over the calculator. "One other name restores the original scale. It doesn't have to be a lover."

{name} looked at the blank. Saying there was no name to borrow would fully expose his weak funding. Deleting the box would reveal the higher price. Taking only the review copy could close today's window. The lead laid the pen flat. "If it isn't a name, decide how much you will give up."

choices.text: State that he brought no name to borrow today
choices.result_text:
"There is no name to borrow for this contract today. Don't write another person down as a possibility."

The deal lead wrote ‘solo’ beside the box and pulled back the gap table. {name}'s weakness opened without declaring any relationship absent.

Only his name and the lower number remained.

choices.text: Delete the co-obligor box and ask its price
choices.result_text:
{name} struck through the box. "What happens to the rate and ceiling if this field does not exist?"

The deal lead produced new figures: higher cost, lower ceiling. "That's the price of going alone."

Another person's name stayed safe and the scale was lost. The old number showed faintly beneath the deletion.

choices.text: Take only the review copy and leave without an answer
choices.result_text:
{name} took the unsigned review copy. "I answer neither the name nor the scale today."

The deal lead opened the door without promising the current terms would remain. {name} surrendered no name and left the window where it stood.

Under the corridor light, the blank box was unnaturally white.

title: A Blank Among the Records
description:
A public terms page, the deal lead's summary, and {name}'s own calculation notes lay together on his desk. All three were currently visible, yet they disagreed about who joint liability covered, its maximum amount, and when it ended.

The public page showed only the liability heading, its scope folded inside a menu. The summary said a name would preserve the terms without saying whose name or what liability. His own name box stayed blank wherever the material failed to agree.

{name} split the available facts from the unknowns. An official inquiry window remained open beside them. He could record why he refused the blank, ask for the scope of the liability language, or state that the mismatched records were why he would not proceed.

choices.text: Write the refusal reason beside the blank in his own notes
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote ‘scope inconsistent; affected person's consent unconfirmed.’ He added no page number or seal missing from the available records.

The reason was clear, but no record reached the other side. A date and the three source labels remained beside the hand-drawn box.

choices.text: Ask the official channel for the scope of joint liability
choices.result_text:
{name} submitted only three questions: who it applied to, maximum exposure, and termination conditions. He did not quote the deal lead's summary as fact.

Only the submission time was confirmed immediately; the three mismatched records remained. Three gaps in his knowledge were exposed, and he invented no document for the empty attachment field.

choices.text: Leave only a non-proceeding reason and close the question draft
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote: ‘I will not proceed while the available records disagree about the liability language and named party.’ He added no claim about receiving or returning any particular document.

The open inquiry window closed, taking the extra-question draft with it. Beneath the sent line there was no new file and no signature.

title: The Night the Bills Arrived
description:
At 11:47 p.m., the Changwon hospital payment window remained open and the tremor in {name}'s fingers had not stopped. The bill was unpaid and no help had been sought for his body. Tonight he had answered Father and let Daeun in when she arrived as promised.

Father said through the call, "Minjun, hear me out first." {name} kept the phone to his ear and looked at Daeun. She placed the review envelope from Sangchul's office on the table without taking off her cardigan.

"Ask whether I may hear the family call, whether we open this envelope now, or what you want me to witness," she said.

Daeun touched neither the payment button nor the help screen. Father's breathing, the sealed envelope, and the shaking hand shared one room, but no unselected action became completed by implication.

choices.text: Ask Daeun whether the call may go on speaker
choices.result_text:
{name} stopped over the speaker icon. "May you hear this? If not, I'll finish outside."

When Daeun nodded, Father's voice entered the room. "Don't send the money first. Hear me out." Daeun did not interrupt.

The privacy of the family call opened; no payment confirmation appeared. Only the speaker icon stayed blue.

choices.text: Hear Father privately, then open the name-review copy to Daeun
choices.result_text:
{name} kept the call off speaker and heard Father to the end. "All right. Tonight I'll listen." After hanging up, he opened the envelope before Daeun.

"Nothing is signed. These are the terms we were reviewing for responsibility." Daeun opened only the joint-liability paragraph. "Then this is all we read tonight."

The family voice stayed private and the contract weakness opened. The bill and help screens remained untouched.

choices.text: Let Daeun ask what she is supposed to witness
choices.result_text:
{name} heard Father to the end and set down the phone. "Ask what you need to confirm tonight. I won't choose the order for you."

Daeun chose no payment or clinic. "Answer three things: is the bill unpaid, is the shaking continuing, and is the envelope still unsigned?" {name} answered yes to each.

Three incomplete facts were visible without handing her the decision. The three screens stayed lit side by side.

title: Three Timestamps
description:
At 11:47 p.m., a payment record opened with its issuer and processing status visible. At 11:51, {name} recorded the tremor in a work note. At 11:56, Jiyeon arrived after his message and stepped inside. Father's name and the running call time showed on the phone.

Jiyeon copied the three times without removing her coat. "I won't combine the facts. The family call record, the contract-review record, and the body signal are different matters."

Father said, "Minjun, are you listening?" Jiyeon asked for neither the speaker nor the contract record. When {name} started to say he was fine, her breath caught half a second late. "I won't decide for you. Separate what you are hiding." The three times were visible; each record kept its current status.

choices.text: Verify all three timestamps with Jiyeon
choices.result_text:
{name} showed the payment record, work note, and entry record in order. Jiyeon read 11:47, 11:51, and 11:56, marking each source differently.

Father ended with, "Hear me out first." Jiyeon recorded that sentence beside the call time.

Three pieces of privacy opened, and no record changed its processing status. Only three source-labeled check marks remained.

choices.text: Keep Father's voice private and open only the contract liability
choices.result_text:
{name} heard Father privately and finished the call. He did not share the audio, opening only the joint-liability language in the contract record currently available.

"I'll own the family words. Help me read my responsibility here." Jiyeon checked only the visible timestamp, source label, and liability language.

Family privacy held and the contract weakness opened. The payment record and body note kept their current status.

choices.text: Ask her to stay until the call ends without processing the open records
choices.result_text:
"Don't process these records for me. Stay until Father finishes."

Jiyeon closed her notes and sat on the chair's edge. Father completed one sentence: "Slow your breathing first." She did not interrupt.

{name} admitted dependence, and all three records kept their current status. Jiyeon's grip on her coat button loosened half a second late.

title: One Call and Open Screens
description:
At 11:47 p.m., the payment page opened. At 11:51, a note about shaking fingers was saved. At 11:55, {name} answered Father. No partner was present, and he had selected neither paying the bill nor seeking help for his body.

"Minjun, are you listening? Hear me out first." A television and the sound of a closing door overlapped faintly behind Father's voice. {name} braced against the sink with the phone to his ear. One side of the laptop held the on-screen issuer and amount; the other held the untreated body signal.

The contact was already completed. Within the call, {name} could disclose the body signal, read the screen's source and amount, or conceal both and keep only the three times in a private record. None of those choices became a payment or clinic arrival.

choices.text: Tell Father the current body signal
choices.result_text:
{name} said his hands were shaking and his vision had briefly doubled. He did not read the bill.

After a breath, Father finished: "Sit down and hear me out first." {name} did not cut the sentence short.

His bodily privacy opened; no help had yet been requested. A shaking line remained beside the 11:55 call record.

choices.text: Read the bill's issuer and amount exactly
choices.result_text:
{name} read the issuing office and every digit on-screen. He did not mention the tremor.

Father completed one sentence: "Don't send that money first. Read the items again." {name} followed the item names without adding an answer.

The money problem opened and the body signal stayed alone. His hand never reached the payment button.

choices.text: Hide both and keep the three times in a private record
choices.result_text:
{name} said only, "I'm listening." Father finished, "It's late in Seoul too. Slow your breathing."

After the call, {name} wrote: 11:47 bill, 11:51 body signal, 11:55 call. He left the source and symptom blank.

Privacy held and no bill closed. Only three times remained on the black screen.
